en: O Buddha, you are supreme; homage to you! Having utterly abandoned all other teachers.
I have gone to you for refuge; you are faultless and endowed with all virtues. 1 [1]
Either the world is devoted to faults, or it perceives faults as virtues,
or it is dull in perceiving virtues.
By which he has gone for refuge to others. [2] [2]
Those qualities which are proclaimed with joy by people through their devotion to Vāsudeva, Īśvara, and others.
Those faults are found within your own teaching. [3] [3]
It is said that when Rudra, enraged, burnt Tripura with a single arrow,
it was actually the fire of his own anger that was consumed.
By you, with the great arrow of knowledge. [4]
For Hara was drawn back again by that ill-burnt Kāma;
yet Kāma has now been offered as an oblation into the fire of your knowledge.
He has gone to destruction along with his very roots. ||5||
Through the amorous charms of Māra’s daughter, you who were armed with a trident became possessed of four faces.
Not even a single hair on his body was curled. [6]
Carrying a woman upon his body, Śaṅkara surpasses even the cakravāka birds with that which is not auspicious; you, however, [surpass him].
He was not at all deluded by desire. || 7 ||
Neither the wielder of the discus nor the wielder of the trident is able to conquer that power of Māra without their discus and trident.
That which has been conquered by you with the weapon of loving-kindness. [8]
Śarva was rendered blue-throated, and Hari was struck by the arrows of old age;
yet you, O Lord, remain beyond all such affliction. 9 [9]
Having assumed the form of a dwarf, Hari deceived Bali through his power of illusion;
you, however, are a knower of illusion.
And you do not deceive others. 10 [10]
O Lord, those by whom Your wondrous leaping across the three worlds was seen have witnessed it like the movement of a cripple.
This is the manifestation of your supernatural powers. ||11||
Even though the prince, together with Ṣaṣṭhī, was practicing celibacy,
he had seven sexual unions with you.
By means of union, they were reduced to ashes. ||12||
"For we are indeed the creators of the world," so it was said by Brahmā and the others;
yet they too, as well as the world, are born of karma.
This was spoken by you, the seer of reality. 13 [13]
It is said that even the wielder of the thunderbolt was deluded by desire upon seeing Ahalyā;
O hero, you have abandoned your wife.
He was utterly deluded by desire alone. ||14||
Soma helplessly becomes the morsel of the elephant Rāhu;
there is no being for whom you [are not food].
Helpless, you shall fall under their control. 15 [15]
Kings such as Rāma and Ambarīṣa returned once more from the forests;
you, however, are satisfied by the nectar of discernment.
Furthermore, O Sugata, he has neither come nor gone. [16]
Those desiring to conquer heaven say that animals are to be sacrificed in the ritual;
yet even the killing of an ant—
But you have not granted me permission, O sinless one. 17 [17]
Seeking women, Rāma indeed went to the far shore of the great ocean,
along with sixty thousand women.
You have gone away, leaving the hermitage behind.
In other sacrifices, others have offered their own lives as clarified butter for their own sake;
but by you alone has it been offered for the sake of others.
The oblations of one's own life have been offered. 19 [18]
Many people have been consumed by the wrathful sages with the fires of their curses;
you, however, have been consumed by the fire of knowledge.
You are the cause of the birth of all people. 20 [19]
The success of the asceticism of the seers is inferred from their power to utter curses;
O Lord, such is the success of your asceticism as well.
It is inferred through the accomplishment of compassion. ||21 [20]||
The linga of Śambhu was cast down by the sages through the curse of one who was lustful;
you have [severed] the root of all misfortunes.
Desire itself has been struck down. 22 [21]
Due to its great length and his failing memory,
the speech of Vyāsa is heard to be internally contradictory, with earlier and later statements at variance.
And yet, O Sage, these do not exist in you at all. [23 (19)]
Generally, those doctrines which were spoken by Dvaipāyana and others have been stated; by you, however, the unique Dharma has been proclaimed.
Having realized it himself, he has revealed it. || 24 [22]||
The Vedas and the words of the heretics are recited only in secluded places,
having proclaimed them with a lion’s roar.
The Dharma is expressed through sound. 25 [23]
Even though he had realized the truth,
Bhāradvāja associated with Vasantī; the wise do not associate with those who are attached.
O Lord, your disciples have been won over by women. ||26 [24]||
"Gifts should be given only to distinguished persons"— thus Kapila has spoken, and not others;
O Lord, [even] to dogs, [gifts] should be given.
This has been spoken by you out of compassion. [27] (25)
The Nirgranthas seek the destruction of their knots through bodily austerities;
you, however, [seek it] through mental austerities.
Do you desire the loosening of the knot? 28 [26]
Logicians desire the establishment of entities as being entirely independent;
yet nothing exists that is not dependent [on something else].
Or has it been said by you, O Vācaspati? [29] [27]
They say that Śuka indeed attained liberation after piercing through the sun;
but you have attained nirvāṇa.
And you have not gone anywhere at all. 30 [28]
Janaka attained liberation by one path, and Śuka went by another;
but you have traveled by whichever path you have gone.
By that very means, those disciples departed. 31 [29]
Viṣṇu had sixteen thousand wives as his consorts;
you, however, are the Teacher, the supreme among men.
Free from pride, free from possessiveness. || 32 [30]||
Vyāsa, though living as a householder, fell into a state of transformation through his passion for Kāśīsundarī; you, however, are like those who are ignoble.
He was not deluded by the objects of the senses. || 33 [31] ||
Vyāsa was afflicted by desire and became distraught when struck by the feet of a woman; you, however, are not like that.
Even when he had become a householder, he was trembling. || 34 [32]||
The slaughter of Karṇa, Duryodhana, and the others was intended by Hari;
even your life-breaths were surrendered by you.
Out of a desire for the welfare of sentient beings.
That earth which was seized by Viṣṇu through three strides after he had employed a stratagem has been abandoned by him like a blade of grass.
By you, who desire liberation. 36 [35]
Having rid the world of the Kṣatriyas with arrows that caused the destruction of living beings,
the fame which Rāma attained—
That brings you ill repute in the treatise. 37 [36]
For whose sake the Kauravas and Pāṇḍavas waged war— her,
who is like a creeper infested with venomous snakes.
Having abandoned prosperity, you have gone forth. || 38 [37] ||
Having received your instruction, [I shall relate] that which was the conduct of the Lord of Yogins in the Devadāru forest of Śambhu.
That is the activity of ignorance. 39 [38]
Even today, Maghavan is sung of by the twice-born for having obtained Ahalyā as the first fruit [of his penance], while you have obtained it as the foremost fruit.
The fame of Śakra has been proclaimed. 40 [39]
It is said that the stainless jīva passes from one body to another;
it is not separate from the body.
"You have stated that the soul exists. [41] [52]
Your own maternal uncle was pierced by the prince with his spear;
O Hero, the web of afflictions has been pierced by you.
It was split open by the power of wisdom. 42 [67]
Indeed, even his own inner apartments were not protected by Viṣṇu for the sake of protecting all sentient beings.
O Sage, you are ever-vigilant. ||43|| [68]||
Knowing the fear of Jarāsaṃdha, Hari abandoned Mathurā;
there is no such being as he.
O Sage, you should be afraid of that from which [you fear]. [44] [69]
The kinsmen of Vāsudeva perished through misconduct;
but all your kinsmen, by you—
They have been completely liberated from cyclic existence. 45 [70]
For Kṛṣṇa,
afflicted by fear of the dark Yavana, entered beneath the bed of Mucukunda.
O Lord, you are fearless in every respect. 46 [40]
Prajāpati desired his own daughter Śruti;
[he practiced] stainless celibacy.
And also for your disciples, O Sage. 47 [41]
The transference of merit and demerit has been declared to be like the receiving of a gift; thus there would be the loss of what was done and the acquisition of what was not done. 48 [42]
The self is conceptualized by the followers of Kapila as having the characteristic of volition;
this has been stated by you regarding the self. [49] [43]
Kaṇāda has proclaimed that the self is distinct from cognition and all-pervading;
[otherwise, it would follow that it is] like a piece of wood. (50) [44]
The individual soul (jīva) is both contracting and expanding, and its size is equal to that of the body;
so says Nagna, because it occupies space.
Its destruction has been explained by you. 51 [45]
The twice-born postulate that the Puruṣa is the eternal cause of the world,
being both eternal and the cause.
"You have said that nothing at all exists. [52] [46]
Kapila consumed with his glance the sixty thousand sons of the high-souled Sagara.
Even there, you possess compassion. [53] [47]
Kapila, the knower of reality, declared that the world was produced from Pradhāna;
birth arises from karma and afflictions.
The nature of the world has been described by you. ||54|| [48]||
Even for Kapila and others, the self remains a cause of rebirth even in liberation;
you, however, have attained that state of peace which is reckoned as final.
You do not go forth like a fire that has been extinguished. || 55 [49] ||
By some Tīrthakaras, liberation has been declared to possess motion;
that which possesses motion is cyclic existence (saṃsāra).
Having understood it, you have made it manifest. || 56 [50]||
The undertaking of gardens and such activities are the causes of sin for the naked ones; indeed,
O Omniscient One, they are exactly so.
Those causes of merit have been explained by you. [57] (51)
In battle, the life-force of Śiśupāla was struck down by Kṛṣṇa;
it did not become separate from the body.
"You have declared that the living being exists. [58] (verse missing)
O Lord, you have described the auspicious destiny for one who dies in battle out of anger as spoken by Vyāsa, yet you have also described a miserable state. [59] (53)
The merit of the sons of Pāṇḍu has been described individually;
now [I shall describe] those who approach women who should not be approached.
They are to be censured according to your teaching. 60 [54]
The more I reflect upon the doctrines of the followers of other sects,
the more my mind is drawn toward you alone.
O Lord, the mind becomes serene. 61 [71]
Thus, those whose intentions are gripped by the perception of faults in the doctrine of one who is not omniscient [reject] even a faultless Teacher.
Those lacking in wisdom do not perceive you. 62 [72]
The world said: "These Śākyas are haters of the Vedas, the gods, and the twice-born;
it is their own fault indeed."
Why does the world not understand this? 63 [73]
Surendra, Upendra, Rudra, and the others always carry their weapons,
whether out of fear or for the purpose of terrifying [others].
You are fearless, and you are not terrifying.
You do not frighten anyone,
nor are you frightened by anyone; for you alone have laid down your weapons.
Therefore, you are superior to the world.
The statements in the Vedas and other scriptures are generally contradicted by what precedes and follows them;
they speak of the affliction of the speaker.
Your speech [proclaims] your omniscience. 66 [57]||
Other treatises are for the most part contradictory from beginning to end,
but this one is consistent in its beginning, middle, and conclusion.
Your opinion is indeed stainless. || 67 [58]||
"One should not give instruction to a Śūdra," so it has been said by those who have mastered the Vedas;
yet, out of compassion, one may even do so for Caṇḍālas.
The true Dharma has been taught by you. 68 [59]
Who would perform what is difficult to do?
Having encountered you who are free from passion, what wise person would bow to other teachers? 69 [60]
Even while enjoying sense objects,
the followers of Kapila are liberated through knowledge;
for one who is afflicted, how could there be liberation?
"You have spoken, O one free from stain. [70] [61]
That which has been spoken by you, O Blessed One, is not stated in other treatises;
having thus completed the accumulation of merit, [one attains the goal].
It is dedicated for the sake of sentient beings. || 71 [62]||
Having caused the oppression of living beings at temples and sacrifices,
worldly people desire merit.
That has been censured by you in the scripture. || 72 [63] ||
Where the slaughter of living beings was certain,
you, O Lord, protected those creatures even at the cost of your own life. [64]
Where truth, non-violence, celibacy, self-restraint, and compassion prevail—
therein is the one born of the Śākya royal lineage.
That dharma is approved by you. 74 [65]
"Even toward an assailant approaching in battle who has mastered the Vedanta,
it has been said by you as well in this world."
Compassion even toward those who would kill. 75 [66]
Since happiness is obtained through happiness alone in your teaching,
therefore, O tiger among speakers, [I take refuge in you].
This person finds delight in this doctrine.
By whatever merit I possess from speaking of your virtues according to this method, may it [be for your benefit].
May the world be equal to you. 77 [75]
By whatever merit has been acquired by me through reciting this *Viśeṣastava*,
may this entire world [attain liberation].
May he be destined for enlightenment. 78 [76]
The *Viśeṣastava* is completed.
Of Bhaṭṭarādhasvāmin.
